==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:adressen|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|adressen|t=to raise erect, adorn}}, from {{der|en|fro|adrecier|t=to straighten, address}} (modern {{cog|fr|adresser}}), from {{der|en|roa-pro|*addīrēctiāre}}, from {{m|la|ad-||to; towards}} + {{m|roa-pro|*dīrēctiāre||to guide; to direct}}, from {{der|en|la|dīrēctus|t=straight; right}}, from {{m|la|dīrigō||to lay straight; to direct}}, itself from {{m|la|regō|t=to govern, to rule}}. Cognate with {{cog|es|aderezar||to garnish; dress (food); to add spices}}.

===Pronunciation===

** {{IPA|en|/əˈdɹɛs/|/ˈædɹɛs/|a=noun}}, {{enPR|ə-drĕsʹ|ăd-rĕsʹ}}
** {{IPA|en|/əˈdɹɛs/|/ˈædɹɛs/|q2=less common|a=verb}}, {{enPR|ə-drĕsʹ|ăd-rĕsʹ}}
* {{a|en|RP}}
** {{IPA|en|/əˈdɹɛs/|/ˈædɹɛs/|q2=rare|a=noun}}, {{enPR|ə-drĕsʹ|ădʹrĕs}}
** {{IPA|en|/əˈdɹɛs/|a=verb}}, {{enPR|ə-drĕsʹ}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-address.ogg|a=US|IPA=/əˈdɹɛs/}}

* {{rhymes|en|ɛs|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{ng|Direction.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[guidance|Guidance]]; [[help]]. {{defdate|15th–17th c.}}
## {{lb|en|chiefly|in plural|now|archaic}} A polite [[approach]] made to another person, especially of a romantic nature; an amorous [[advance]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1723|author=w:Richard Steele|title=The Lover and Reader|page=115
|passage=[H]e was thus agreeable, and I neither insensible of his Perfections, nor displeased at his '''Addresses''' to me {{...}}.}}
## A manner of speaking or writing to another; [[language]], [[style]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
##: {{co|en|a man of pleasing or insinuating '''address'''}}
## {{senseid|en|formal approach}} {{lb|en|diplomacy|politics}} A formal approach to a [[sovereign]] or [[head of state]], especially an official [[appeal]] or [[petition]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
### {{lb|en|Commonwealth|politics}} A response given by each of the [[Houses of Parliament]] to the sovereign's speech at the opening of Parliament.
## {{senseid|en|speech}} An act of addressing oneself to a person or group; a [[discourse]] or [[speech]], or a record of this. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1887|author=w:Arthur Conan Doyle|title=A Study in Scarlet|section=VII
|passage=Mr. Gregson, who had listened to this '''address''' with considerable impatience, could contain himself no longer.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1889|author=Margaret Oliphant|title=The Portrait
|passage=I watched her without knowing, with a prevision that she was going to address me, though with no sort of idea as to the subject of her '''address'''.}}
## {{senseid|en|description}} A description of the location of a property, usually with at least a street name and number, name of a town, and now also a postal code; such a description as superscribed for direction on an envelope or letter. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-14|author=w:Jonathan Freedland
|volume=189|issue=1|page=18|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/2013/jun/07/obama-apple-google-facebook-tainted-prism Obama's once hip brand is now tainted]
|passage=Where we once sent love letters in a sealed envelope, or stuck photographs of our children in a family album, now such private material is despatched to servers and clouds operated by people we don't know and will never meet. Perhaps we assume that our name, '''address''' and search preferences will be viewed by some unseen pair of corporate eyes, probably not human, and don't mind that much.}}
##: {{ux|en|The President's '''address''' is 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue NW in Washington, D.C.}}
## {{senseid|en|location}} The location of a property. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|I went to his '''address''' but there was nobody there.}}
## {{senseid|en|memory}} {{lb|en|computing}} A number identifying a specific storage location in computer [[memory]]. {{defdate|from 1940s}}
##: {{ux|en|The program will crash if there is no valid data stored at that '''address'''.}}
## {{senseid|en|networking}} {{lb|en|networking|Internet}} A [[string]] of [[character]]s identifying a [[node]] or [[range]] of nodes on a [[network]] (especially the [[Internet]]), such as an [[e-mail address]], [[IP address]] or [[URL]]. {{defdate|from 1960s}}
##: {{syn|en|network address}}
# {{ng|Preparation.}}
## {{lb|en|now|rare}} [[preparedness|Preparedness]] for some task; [[resourcefulness]]; [[skill]], [[ability]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1777|author=w:Richard Brinsley Sheridan|title=The School for Scandal|section=V.i
|passage=This is one bad effect of a good Character—it invites applications from the unfortunate and there needs no small degree of '''address''' to gain the reputation of Benevolence without incurring the expence.—}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1789|author={{w|John Moore (Scottish physician)|John Moore}}|title=Zeluco|publisher=Valancourt|year_published=2008|page=129
|passage=The warmth of Father Pedro's constitution had formerly drawn him into some scrapes from which it required all his '''address''' to disengage himself, and rendered him exceedingly cautious ever after.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1813|chapter=Customs, Manners, and present Appearance of Constantinople|title=The New Annual Register, or General Repository of History, Politics, and Literature for the year 1812|pageurl=http://books.google.ca/books?id=MXwEAAAAQAAJ&dq=pedipulation&q=pedipulations#v=snippet&q=pedipulations&f=false|page=179
|passage=At their turning-lathes, they employ their toes to guide the chisel; and, in these pedipulations, shew to Europeans a diverting degree of '''address'''.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete}} The act of getting ready; [[preparation]]. {{defdate|17th–18th c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1671|author=w:John Milton|title=Samson Agonistes
|passage=But now again she makes '''address''' to speak.}}
## {{lb|en|golf|Scotland}} The act of bringing the head of the [[club]] up to the [[ball]] in preparation for swinging. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}<ref name=DSL>{{R:DSL|pos=v., n}}</ref>

===Verb===
{{rfc|en}}
{{en-verb|+|+|+,addrest<l:obsolete>}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To prepare oneself.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Troilus and Cressida|act=II|scene=ii|page=616<!--url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uNtBAQAAMAAJ&pg=RA1-PA242-->| passage=Let us '''address''' to tend on Hector's heels.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[direct#Verb|direct]] [[speech]].
#* {{RQ:Dryden Virgil|chapter=Virgil’s Æneis, Book VII|page=402
|passage=Young ''Turnus'' to the Beaubteous Maid '''addreſs’d'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[aim]]; to [[direct#Verb|direct]].
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|I|X|text=And this good knight his way with me '''addrest'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[prepare]] or make [[ready]].
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=IV|canto=III|stanza=14|passage=His foe was soone '''addrest'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Dryden Virgil|chapter=Virgil’s Æneis, Book X|page=517
|passage=Then ''Turnus'', from his chariot, leaping light, '''Addreſs’d''' himſelf on foot to ſingle fight.}}
#* {{RQ:Taylor Great Exemplar|passage=The five foolish virgins '''addressed''' themselves at the noise of the bridegroom's coming.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|reflexive}} To prepare oneself; to apply one's skill or energies (to some object); to betake.
#* {{RQ:Macaulay History of England|chapter=6|passage=These men '''addressed''' themselves to the task.}}
#* {{RQ:Melville Moby-Dick|[[s:Moby-Dick (1851) US edition/Chapter 3|chapter 3]]|text={{...}} good heavens! dumplings for supper! One young fellow in a green box coat, '''addressed''' himself to these dumplings in a most direful manner.}}
# {{lb|en|reflexive}} To [[direct]] one’s [[remark]]s (''to'' someone).
#* {{RQ:Swift Gulliver|part=I|page=30|passage=There were ſeveral of his Prieſts and Lawyers preſent, (as I conjectured by their habits) who were commanded to '''addreſs''' themſelves to me, and I ſpoke to them in as many Languages as I had the leaſt ſmattering of, which were ''High'' and ''Low Dutch'', ''Latin'', ''French'', ''Spaniſh'', ''Italian'', and ''Lingua Franca''; but all to no purpoſe.}}
#* {{RQ:Austen Pride and Prejudice|I|11|text=He '''addressed''' himself directly to Miss Bennet, with a polite congratulation {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1876|author=w:Henry Martyn Robert|title=w:Robert’s Rules of Order|location=Chicago|publisher=S.C. Griggs & Co.|section=p. 66, Article V, Section 34|url=http://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/9097/pg9097-images.html
|passage=When any member is about to speak in debate, he shall rise and respectfully '''address''' himself to “Mr. Chairman.”}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To [[clothe]] or [[array]]; to [[dress]].
#: {{syn|en|beclothe|dight|put on|Thesaurus:clothe}}
# {{tea room sense|en|m=March|y=2020}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To direct, as words (''to'' anyone or anything); to make, as a speech, petition, etc. (''to'' any audience).
#* {{RQ:Dryden Virgil|chapter=Dedication [of the Æneis]|page=187
|passage=though the young Heroe had '''addreſs’d''' his Prayers to him for his aſſiſtance}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''addressed''' some portions of his remarks to his supporters, some to his opponents.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To direct speech to; to make a communication to, whether spoken or written; to [[apply]] to by words, as by a speech, petition, etc., to [[speak to]].
#* {{RQ:Addison Cato|20|passage=Are not your orders to '''address''' the senate?}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1724|author=w:Jonathan Swift|chapter=w:Drapier's Letters|title=[[s:The Works of the Rev. Jonathan Swift/Volume 9/The Drapier’s Letters 3|3]]
|passage=The representatives of the nation in parliament, and the privy council, '''address''' the king}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1989|author=w:Grant Naylor|title={{w|Red Dwarf}}: {{w|Infinity Welcomes Careful Drivers}}|text=Rimmer paused for no discernible reason, then yelled, equally inexplicably: 'Shut up!', wheeled round 180º, and appeared to be '''addressing''' a dartboard.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-07-19|author=w:Peter Wilby| volume=189| issue=6| page=30| magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly| title=[http://www.theguardian.com/education/2013/jul/01/education-michael-gove-finland-gcse Finland spreads word on schools]| passage=Imagine a country where children do nothing but play until they start compulsory schooling at age seven. Then, without exception, they attend comprehensives until the age of 16. {{...}} Children '''address''' teachers by their first names. Even 15-year-olds do no more than 30 minutes' homework a night.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To direct in writing, as a letter; to [[superscribe]], or to direct and [[transmit]].
#: {{ux|en|He '''addressed''' a letter.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To make [[suit]] to as a lover; to [[court]]; to [[woo]].
#: {{syn|en|romance|put the moves on|Thesaurus:woo}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[consign]] or [[entrust]] to the care of another, as agent or factor.
#: {{ux|en|The ship was '''addressed''' to a merchant in Baltimore.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To address oneself to; to prepare oneself for; to apply oneself to; to direct one's speech, discourse or efforts to.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1990|author=Stephen King|title={{w|The Moving Finger (short story)|The Moving Finger}}
|passage=He stepped away from the sink, put up the toilet ring (Vi complained bitterly if he forgot to put it down when he was through, but never seemed to feel any pressing need to put it back up when ''she'' was), and '''addressed''' the John.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|formal}} To direct attention towards a problem or obstacle, in an attempt to [[resolve]] it.
#: {{syn|en|speak to|field|q2=(a question or problem)}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=April 19, 2012|author=Josh Halliday| title=Free speech haven or lawless cesspool – can the internet be civilised?| url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/technology/2012/apr/19/free-speech-haven-lawless-cesspool| passage="By all means we want people to use social media, but we do not want you to use it in ways that will incite violence," said Jonathan Toy, Southwark council's head of community safety. "This remains a big issue for us and without some form of censorship purely focusing on [violent videos], I'm not sure how we can '''address''' it."}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2020 December 2|author=Mark Phillips|title=Rebuilding Rail in the 2020s|journal=Rail|page=46|text=Formerly [sic: Formally] known as the {{w|Rail Safety and Standards Board}}, the not-for-profit organisation's remit includes managing and developing Railway Group Standards on behalf of the rail industry, leading the development of long-term safety strategy, and supporting cross-industry groups that '''address''' major areas of safety risk.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|computing}} To refer to a location in computer memory.
# {{lb|en|transitive|golf|Scotland}} To get ready to hit (the [[ball]] on the [[tee]]).<ref name=DSL>{{R:DSL|pos=v., n}}</ref>

====Usage notes====
* The intransitive uses can be understood as omission of the reflexive pronoun.
